cases.purpose: tetris restores the private terminal after SIGINT.
cases.stdout:
observer-control=PASS
raw-mode=PASS
signal-delivered=PASS
child-exited=PASS
termios-restored=PASS
cursor-shown=PASS
cases.oracle: Documented terminal restoration contract; a fresh private PTY and an owned session leader. Setup checks the observer against a separate raw-mode stub for each signal. Only the child created by the observer is signalled, and only inside the disposable VM.
cases.comparison: Wait for raw terminal readiness, signal that owned child, retain raw output, signal event, natural status and termios; cursor-show is required for tetris. Raw live termios, the owned child identity, sent signal or byte, and cleanup status are retained.

cases.purpose: A lone ESC reports ESCAPE after the documented 50ms continuation grace.
cases.stdout:
observer-control=PASS
raw-mode=PASS
escape-record=PASS
grace-window=PASS
child-exited=PASS
termios-restored=PASS
cases.oracle: The documented lone-ESC 50ms continuation grace; a monotonic observer uses a 30-500ms acceptance window. Separate fast and 50ms stub controls validate the timing gate.
cases.comparison: Retains raw bytes, measured monotonic elapsed time and initial/final termios; scheduling beyond the tolerance is a fixture qualification issue. Raw live termios, the owned child identity, sent signal or byte, and cleanup status are retained.

cases.purpose: Seeded interactive tetris left follows the geometric or pause contract.
cases.stdout:
observer-control=PASS
geometry=PASS
four-cells=PASS
transition=PASS
quit-status=PASS
terminal-restored=PASS
cursor-shown=PASS
cases.oracle: Four-cell geometric invariants: j/l shift one column; k rotates a nonsymmetric tetromino counterclockwise, up to translation; p freezes a known advancing piece and p resumes it. The 20x10 well and seed are fixed. A separately constructed ECMA-48 screen and hand-specified shape are the observer control; headless game output is never used.
cases.comparison: Retains decoded cell coordinates, directional input timing, raw frame bytes, final score/status, cursor and termios. Gravity baseline is required before testing pause. Every sent PTY byte and its monotonic timestamp and capture offset are retained.

cases.purpose: The password remains hidden at every decoded terminal output byte and is returned on the result fd.
cases.stdout:
observer-control=PASS
ready=PASS
baseline-clean=PASS
result=PASS
status=PASS
restored=PASS
no-leak=PASS
cases.oracle: Pinned newt whiptail 0.52.25 and its passwordbox no-display contract. The synthetic password uses characters absent from the initial frame; the observer feeds every terminal output byte to pyte and checks every screen state. Setup requires a masked stub to pass and a deliberately leaking stub to be detected.
cases.comparison: Both sides must return the entered value (a single optional trailing newline is accepted), return 0, restore termios and never render any secret character; raw output, result bytes and detected leak offsets are retained.
